status: Explicit exact analytic sharpness family, not an empirical test
domain: Unit flat torus; planar disk strictly inside its first two coordinates

family.A_planar: Lambda e_r e_r^T + lambda e_theta e_theta^T in the disk; any matrix in the same eigenvalue interval outside
family.A_extra: lambda times the identity in any extra coordinates
family.eta: Any smooth radial cutoff equal to one near r=0 and zero before the disk boundary
family.u: eta u0, adjusted by its torus mean if necessary
family.F_planar: u0 A_planar grad(eta) - psi J grad(eta), J=[[0,-1],[1,0]]
family.extra_coordinate_dependence: All fields independent of the extra torus coordinates

exact_identity: A grad(u)-F=J grad(eta psi) in the first two components and zero in the others; hence div(A grad u)=div F
integrability: u is an energy solution, F is smooth, and grad(u) is not in L^p for p >= p_upper
failed_claim_upper: A universal L^p gradient estimate for the energy solution follows from only these ellipticity bounds for p >= p_upper
failed_claim_lower: A universal L^p bound for the same energy-solution gradient operator holds for 1 < p <= p_lower
lower_scope_reason: The symmetric energy-solution operator is self-adjoint; boundedness below p_lower would imply boundedness above p_upper by duality
scope: Sharpness of the uniform exponent interval for this scalar symmetric elliptic coefficient class. It is not a lower bound for discrete optimization or for all numerical PDE algorithms.
